title: Quick Korean Lean Ground Beef Rice Bowl
description: Flavorful Korean-style ground beef served over warm jasmine rice with a sweet-savory garlic soy sauce. Quick, high-protein meal prep ready in 25 minutes.
steps: Combine 1 1/2 cups (300 g) rinsed jasmine rice and 2 cups (475 ml) water in a saucepan over high heat. Bring to a boil, then cover, turn heat to low, and simmer for 12 to 15 minutes until water is absorbed and rice is tender.

Whisk 1/3 cup (80 ml) reduced-sodium soy sauce, 2 tablespoons (25 g) brown sugar, 1 tablespoon (15 ml) sesame oil, 1 tablespoon (15 g) gochujang, 4 minced garlic cloves, and 1 tablespoon (6 g) grated ginger in a bowl for 1 minute until smooth and sugar dissolves.

Heat a 12-inch nonstick skillet over medium-high heat for 2 minutes. Add 1 1/2 lbs (680 g) lean ground beef and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking into small crumbles with a spatula, until browned and an instant-read thermometer registers 160°F (71°C).
Pour the sauce mixture over the cooked beef in the skillet over medium heat. Stir constantly for 2 to 3 minutes until the sauce bubbles, thickens, and evenly coats the ground beef.
Fluff the rice with a fork and divide among 4 bowls. Top each with one-quarter of the Korean beef, garnish with sliced green onions and sesame seeds, and serve hot.
tips: Use 93/7 or leaner ground beef to keep protein high without excess saturated fat.
For extra micronutrients, stir 2 cups of fresh spinach into the beef during the last minute of simmering until wilted.
storage: Store beef and rice in airtight containers in the refrigerator for up to 4 days.

steps_short: Whisk together soy sauce, brown sugar, gochujang, garlic, and ginger.
Brown lean ground beef until cooked to 160 degrees Fahrenheit.
Pour sauce into the skillet and simmer until nicely glazed.
Serve over fluffy jasmine rice with sliced green onions and sesame seeds.

issues: The water-to-rice ratio is too high: 3 cups (710 ml) of water for 1 1/2 cups (300 g) of rinsed jasmine rice (1:2 ratio) will result in mushy, waterlogged rice. Jasmine rice requires a lower liquid-to-rice ratio, typically 1:1.33 to 1:1.5 (2 cups / 475 ml water for 1 1/2 cups rinsed rice).
